title: Oklahoma 14, Nebraska 13: Bud Wilkinson's First Lincoln Trip
question: What was the score when Bud Wilkinson's first Oklahoma team played at Nebraska in 1947?
answer: Oklahoma beat Nebraska 14-13 in Lincoln on November 22, 1947, in Bud Wilkinson's first season as head coach. The Sooners finished 7-2-1 and shared the Big Six title with Kansas.
summary: On November 22, 1947, Bud Wilkinson's first Oklahoma team edged Nebraska 14-13 in snowy Lincoln, on the way to a shared Big Six title.
body: Oklahoma's football story changed course in 1947. Jim Tatum had left after one season, and Bud Wilkinson, at just 31, took over as head coach and athletic director. By late November his first Sooner team had a Big Six title within reach, and the schedule sent it to Lincoln on November 22 to face Nebraska at Memorial Stadium.

The trip came in snowy weather, and the game was close from start to finish. Scoring by quarter shows both teams scoreless in the first period, then Oklahoma leading 7-6 at halftime before the two sides traded touchdowns in the third quarter. Neither team scored in the fourth, so the one-point margin held.

When it ended, Oklahoma had the narrowest of wins, 14-13, over a Nebraska team that would finish just 2-7. For a coach opening what became one of the great runs in the sport, it was an early reminder that championships often turn on a single point.

That season ended with Oklahoma at 7-2-1 overall and 4-0-1 in conference play, tied with Kansas atop the Big Six standings. It was only the start. The Sooners went on to win 14 straight conference championships from 1946 through 1959, with Wilkinson at the helm for 13 of them. Looking back, that snowy afternoon in Lincoln was a small, one-point step on the way to a dynasty.
